title: Plugin Split Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan · thirteen steps under the issue "Split house-rules into nine plugins and a shared library" (#437)

short.lead: You approved the design as "Design approved: plugin split 1* 2A 3A 4A 5A 6A 7A 8A". Your own answer to choice 1 on the design page adds a ninth plugin, Accessible AI. These are the thirteen steps, each a GitHub issue under #437 that names what it depends on and when it is done. The order puts the risky unknowns first: step 1 proves that plugins can depend on each other before anything moves. Every step that moves a part also turns that part's reminders, report-only checks and text-only rules into checks that refuse. The target layout is in docs/4-systems/plugin-split.md.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it moves and when it counts as done.
items: Prove that plugins can depend on each other and that several end-of-reply hooks can work together (#438)
Two throwaway plugins test whether one plugin's dependencies field installs another, and what happens when two plugins block the same reply.
The shared library plugin, with no hooks of its own (#439)
The plumbing and the page builder move into a plugin that cannot refuse anything.
The Rule enforcement plugin and the repeat-failure lock (#440)
Rule injection moves, a lock is built that refuses edits after a check has blocked three times, and the 21 off switches are removed.
safe_git.py and the work-saving hooks move. A new check refuses local paths in issues, and the guard on waiting commands, removed by the guard-friction issue (#292), is reworked.
docs.py, the archivist, doc-ref and the plain-docs check move. The docs reminder at commit time starts refusing.
The standards move, YAGNI, KISS and DRY are written in by name, and checks for what can be measured are added.
The evidence check, the stale-memory warning and the machine profile move. A docs-freshness check is new.
The Check your work plugin, with screenshot and video tools (#445)
The proof rules, the visual check, handovers and the reviewer move. Screenshot and video tools and a review that must pass before "done" are new.
The No hiding plugin, with a research-citation check (#446)
Audits, ledgers and the stall check move. A check that research cites sources with quotes is new.
design_loop.py moves. The page check and the refusal of shell writes while code is locked only report today; both start refusing.
The writing checks, the editor and the voice move. The features for ADHD, autism and dyslexia get their own design page first.
Approve that design page when it comes.
The delegation rule, the scout, builder and reviewer helpers, and the two-helper limit join the existing router plugin.
Install tooling for many plugins, and retire house-rules (#450)
The install and update tools handle every plugin, and house-rules is uninstalled so no rule runs twice.
You test it on your PC.

changes: The library and nine plugins, each in its own folder beside house-rules, listed in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json.
Each plugin ships on its own and moves its part out of house-rules in the same release, under choice 2.
Each plugin's tests come from the matching file already in scripts/checks/, so no check is lost.
The existing offshoot plugin gains the delegation rule, the scout, builder and reviewer helpers, and the two-helper limit.
It nudges a prompt toward a model-pinned helper.
It also holds the delegation rule and enforces the helper limit.
The issue "restructure into a shared core with project boundaries and six optional sub-plugins" describes the plan this one replaces.
Open, with its 2.74.0 build reverted in pull request #428.
Its branch AjsAgent/issue-281-fix stays as a source to reuse code from.
choices: loop
Choice 1: does the Design loop become part of Accessible AI?
A
No, it stays its own plugin
Accessible AI depends on it instead. Keeping the 2,281-line loop separate matches the reason for the split: smaller pieces are easier to maintain.
B
Yes, fold it into Accessible AI
One plugin for the whole think, design and plan flow, as your answer suggested, but it becomes the largest plugin.
Your answer to choice 1 said the design loop "could also fit here as well", which could mean keeping it separate or folding it in.
migrate
Choice 2: how do the plugins replace house-rules?
A
One at a time
Each release ships one plugin and deletes the same part from house-rules, so every release can be tested and reverted alone.
B
All at once
One release swaps everything. This is how 2.74.0 shipped, and it was reverted.
This decides how many releases the split takes and what each QA pass covers.
old
Choice 3: what happens to the earlier restructure issue (#306)?
A
Close it as replaced by #437
A comment names #437 as the plan that replaces it.
B
Leave it open
Two open parents describe the same work.
Its open sub-issues would be closed or moved under #437 the same way.

wrapup.summary: Thirteen steps, one GitHub issue each (#438 to #450) under #437, starting with a test that plugins can depend on each other.
wrapup.changing: Nothing in the plugin yet. The new files are this page, docs/4-systems/plugin-split.md and two entries in docs/6-decisions/Decisions.md.
wrapup.blocking: Your approval of this plan and your answers to the three choices.
wrapup.next: I start step 1 (#438), the test of plugin dependencies.
